title: How the Tesla Roadster Hangs Upside Down
description:
The new Tesla Roadster hangs upside down because fans pull the air out from under the car while skirts seal the gap, so the outside air pins it to the ramp. Tesla says that push reaches up to twice the car's weight, and it holds even when the car is standing still. Then jets of compressed gas roll it the right way up before it lands. The trick itself isn't new: racing officials banned the Chaparral 2J's fans after the 1970 season.

title: The Tesla Roadster's 0.81 Second Launch
description:
Gas jets fired the new Tesla Roadster from 0 to 60 mph in 0.81 seconds at its 15 October demo, about half the time of a Rimac Nevera R (1.66 s, independently timed by Dewesoft). But the stopwatch was Tesla's own, and nobody outside the company has timed the car yet. Musk says the production car will be quicker still. Tesla's own claims by version: Rocket (off-road) under 0.59 s, Thrust under 1 s, Performance under 1.6 s. The 3.4 g on screen is our own arithmetic (60 mph in 0.81 s).

Footage: Tesla, "The 0-60 | Roadster" (YouTube, 16 Oct 2026), slowed 8x with frame interpolation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zg9Q56t7bdo

title: How Long Can the Tesla Roadster Fly?
description:
The new Tesla Roadster's flying trick runs on two carbon-wrapped tanks holding about a quarter of a tonne of compressed gas. By our own estimate, the rear nozzles at full power would empty them in about two seconds. Tesla told Top Gear the Thrust version gets a single launch per fill, and that a refill from a high-pressure nitrogen rig takes 2-6 hours today. On stage, Musk said the car can refill its own tank.

Our estimate: about 80 kN of thrust divided by gas leaving at roughly 600 m/s is about 130 kg a second, so about 250 kg lasts about 2 seconds at full thrust; hovering needs far less push, so 8-11 seconds at best.

Footage: Tesla, "The Kickflip | Roadster" (YouTube, 16 Oct 2026), slowed 10x with frame interpolation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r5vsHHPVhJg
The x-ray of the tanks and nozzles is our own 3D illustration, not Tesla footage.

Sources:
